input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—do you need my date of birth too?

I can see that my phone shows a good signal and says "5G" at the top, and I think mobile data is turned on. Regular calls and normal text messages seem to work fine—it's just the picture messages that won't send. What should I do next?
I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next?

I found something called "APN Name" set to "internet" and an "MMSC URL" that says "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." Is that what you needed to know? I’m not sure what any of that means—should I change anything, or is it okay as it is?

I’ve reset the APN settings as you suggested. I’m a bit nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Could you reassure me before I go ahead and reboot?
Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—this is taking longer than I expected.

I haven’t noticed any error messages—it just keeps trying to send and never goes through. As for using the internet or other apps with Wi-Fi off, I’m not sure how to check that. Could you tell me how to see if my phone is using mobile data instead of Wi-Fi?
I turned off Wi-Fi like you said, but it looks like I can’t get on the internet at all—nothing loads. Does this mean my mobile data isn’t working properly? What should I do next?

Oh, I see! I’d rather not change my plan, but I’m okay with adding more data if that will fix the problem. Could you please add 2GB for me? And just to double-check, that will be $4.00, right? I want to make sure before we go ahead.
Yes, please go ahead and add the 2GB for $4.00. I hope this will let me send picture messages again!

I tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. Is there something else I should try, or do I need to restart my phone again now that I have more data? I just want to make sure I’m doing the right thing.
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried that something’s really wrong.
I checked, and it looks like my messaging app only has permission for the phone—it doesn’t mention storage or SMS. Should I add those permissions? If so, could you walk me through how to do that?
I’ve added both storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, and now it looks like I can send picture messages again! Thank you so much for your help and patience—I really appreciate it.
Thank you so much for your help and for being so patient with me. I really appreciate it! Have a wonderful day. ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

First, could you let me know:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send/receive standard text messages (SMS) without any issues?

I can see that my phone shows a good signal and says "5G" at the top, and I think mobile data is turned on. Regular calls and normal text messages seem to work fine—it's just the picture messages that won't send. What should I do next?

Thank you for the details. Since your calls, texts, and mobile data are working, but MMS (picture messages) are not, let’s check a few settings that commonly cause this issue.

Please follow these steps on your phone:

1. Check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS. Could you check if Wi-Fi Calling is ON? If it is, please turn it OFF and try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if you need instructions on how to check or turn off Wi-Fi Calling, or if you’ve already tried this step. If MMS still doesn’t work after this, we’ll move to the next troubleshooting step.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next?

Thank you for checking that. The next step is to verify your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN or missing MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) settings are a common cause of MMS issues.

Could you please check your APN settings and let me know if you see an MMSC URL listed? If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through the process. Let me know what you find, or if you’d like step-by-step instructions.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I found something called "APN Name" set to "internet" and an "MMSC URL" that says "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." Is that what you needed to know? I’m not sure what any of that means—should I change anything, or is it okay as it is?

Thank you for providing those details. Your APN Name and MMSC URL appear to be set, which is good. Since those settings look correct, let’s try another common fix: resetting your APN settings to default, as sometimes even correct-looking settings can have hidden issues.

Here’s what you should do next:
1. Reset your APN settings to the default values on your phone.
2. After resetting, please reboot (restart) your device.

Once your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if you need instructions on how to reset your APN settings or reboot your device, or if you encounter any issues during these steps.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I’ve reset the APN settings as you suggested. I’m a bit nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Could you reassure me before I go ahead and reboot?

Restarting (rebooting) your phone is a safe process and will not delete any of your photos, messages, or other personal data. It simply turns your phone off and back on to refresh its system and apply any changes you’ve made, such as resetting APN settings.

You will not lose any important information by restarting your device. Once your phone is back on, you can try sending a picture message again.

Please go ahead and reboot your phone. Let me know if you have any concerns or if you need help with the restart process.

To check if your phone is using mobile data instead of Wi-Fi, please follow these steps:

1. Turn off Wi-Fi on your phone. You can usually do this by swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings panel and tapping the Wi-Fi icon so it’s no longer highlighted.
2. Once Wi-Fi is off, look at the top of your screen. You should see an icon like “5G,” “4G,” “LTE,” or similar, which means your phone is connected to mobile data.
3. Open your web browser or any app that requires internet (like email or social media) and try to load a webpage or refresh your feed.

Let me know if you’re able to access the internet with Wi-Fi turned off. This will help us confirm that your mobile data connection is working, which is necessary for sending MMS.

Yes, your messaging app needs both storage and SMS permissions to send and receive picture messages (MMS). Please add both permissions for your messaging app.

Here’s how you can do it on most Android phones:
1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and select your messaging app from the list.
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Enable both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions.

If you’re using an iPhone, permissions are usually managed automatically, but you can check under Settings > [Your Messaging App] > Permissions.

Once you’ve enabled both permissions, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you need more help!
